identity_evidence.quote: An 84-year-old man developed an intermittent cough of unknown etiology in early February 2024

attribution_limitations: Timing of the AAV diagnosis: the abstract says AAV and ANCA-associated nephritis had been diagnosed for more than 9 months, but the main text diagnoses AAV on the basis of the February 18 serology during this admission and says nephritis was not excluded.
The discussion cites skin photographs as Fig. 4G and H, but panels G and H belong to Figure 1; Figure 4 shows C3 and C4 counts.

Methylprednisolone tablet dates and doses differ between Table 1 (36 mg from March 18, 32 mg from April 1, 28 mg from April 7) and the Figure 2 annotation (reduced to 36 mg on April 2, 32 mg on the 8th, 28 mg on the 15th); the text says tapering from 40 mg to 8 mg while Table 1 ends at 4 mg.
Garbled printed laboratory values on February 15: hemoglobin "10^(3) g/L↓", lymphocyte "0.1271" and antithrombin III "67%1".
"On the same day" for the creatinine 653 and urea 33.2 values follows the antibiotic adjustment sentence, which has no date of its own; the preceding sentence mentions the February 19 chest CT.
The initial methylprednisolone dose is described as reduced from 60–40 mg in the first 2 weeks, while Table 1 starts at 40 mg on February 26 and the text starts oral glucocorticoids on February 26.
CRRT frequency is "every other day for 8 hours" in phase 3 and "biweekly CRRT sessions" in the results sentence.

The text says the B lymphocyte count remained at 0 from March 8 onward, while the Figure 3 chart prints 0.04 on 2024/4/8 (pixels viewed in the visual submission); the caption and text give no unit or reference range.
The text describes the glucocorticoid plus cyclophosphamide regimen with myelosuppression; the drug causing the cytopenia is not individually attributed.
Discussion sentences about hypogammaglobulinemia, infection rates after rituximab, guideline recommendations and PLEX literature describe cohorts or recommendations, not this patient.
The May 23 sentence ends "for infection prophylaxis" after both mycophenolate mofetil and compound sulfamethoxazole; whether the stated purpose covers mycophenolate mofetil is not clear.

(C) On March 6th, the lesions in both lungs showed improvement compared to the previous status, while the pleural effusion increased. (D) On March 22nd, both lungs demonstrated further improvement, but the pleural effusion augmented. (E) On May 4th, the patchy and reticular density-increased shadows in both lungs were absorbed, and the pleural effusion significantly decreased. (F) On June 19th, a ground-glass density faint patchy shadow was identified in the posterior segment of the left upper lung apex, considering an inflammatory lesion. (G) Multiple large ecchymoses were present throughout the body. (H) Scattered petechiae were found on double upper limbs. CT = computed tomography.
